sites: src/evp/legacy_blake2.rs:191 blake2s_int_init (same class; not a V1 obligation; current 278)
defect.reachability: EVP_MD_meth_get_init (src/evp/digest.rs:1565; libcrypto.ld:1886) returns the callback to any C caller. A fresh EVP_MD_CTX_new() is zero-filled, so md_data is NULL; a NULL ctx dereferences NULL as well.

reproduction.before_fix_candidate: cargo test --lib legacy_blake2b_init -- --test-threads=4: the test panicked at src/digest/blake2.rs:249 with 'null pointer dereference occurred' and the process aborted (SIGABRT, exit 101).
reproduction.before_fix_authority: Four one-process C probes against the pinned 3.6.4 install (BLAKE2b-512/BLAKE2s-256 x {fresh EVP_MD_CTX_new(), NULL ctx}); each printed md_data=(nil) or ctx=NULL and died with exit 139 (SIGSEGV) in the initialiser write.
reproduction.after_fix_candidate: The focused tests return 0 for both fault shapes and 1 for the bound table path; BLAKE2b-512(abc) and BLAKE2s-256(abc) match the pinned authority vectors.

fix.shape: blake2b_int_init and blake2s_int_init now call a private init_md_data(ctx, owner, size) before writing. The helper refuses (None) when ctx is NULL, md_data is NULL, digest is NULL, or the context is bound to a different method whose ctx_size is smaller than the BLAKE2 context; otherwise it returns the block. A refusal answers 0, the C initialise failure value, touching no memory.
fix.normal_path: a context bound to the callback's own table object, or to a method with ctx_size >= size_of::<blake2b::Ctx>() / <blake2s::Ctx>(), still calls ossl_blake2*_init and returns 1; digest maths and result values are unchanged.
fix.authority_comparison: §17 divergence, not compatibility: the authority performs the NULL write and faults; the crate returns 0 on exactly the shapes where the authority does not return.

classes.name: dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, literal) edges resolved by evidence

classes.name: Rust std/core trait-object and internal function-pointer dispatch resolved by evidence
classes.evidence_class: compiler-constructed trait-object vtables and std/core-internal function pointers (panic hook, Once initializer, libc/syscall weak pointers, backtrace callback) inside monomorphized core/std code
classes.resolved_target_set: the linked std/core implementation: impls of core::fmt::Write, core::fmt::Debug, core::ops::Drop and std::io::Write; the installed panic hook; the Once initializer; the libc syscall/open64/set_permissions/getrandom entry points; the libunwind trace callback. classes.name: link-time-constant OpenSSL table edges resolved by evidence
